rag_responses.question: What is the difference between belt drive and direct drive compressors?
rag_responses.answer:
Belt‑drive compressors use a ribbed single or V‑belt to transfer power from the motor to the airend, while direct‑drive compressors couple the motor directly to the airend, eliminating the belt.  

- Belt‑drive models (SX, SM, SK, AS, SFC) feature a unique automatic tensioner that maintains optimal belt tension, prolongs belt life, and allows easy verification through a service‑panel window.  
- Direct‑drive models (ASD, HSD, SFC Direct Drive) provide maximum power transfer and efficiency from motor to airend, run at lower speeds, and have fewer components, reducing heat, drive losses, maintenance, and downtime.

rag_responses.question: Which refrigerant do the integrated dryers use, and why was it chosen?
rag_responses.answer: The integrated dryers use the refrigerant **R‑513A**. It was chosen because it has **56 % lower global warming potential** than common dryer refrigerants and, combined with the advanced heat‑exchanger design, allows the dryer to use **only half the refrigerant** needed, making it the most climate‑friendly dryer possible.

Optimized air flow design
Air is drawn into separate cooling zones for the drive motor and coolers. This "split cooling" design eliminates preheating, increasing cooling efficiency without increasing power consumption. Cooler temperatures also promote longer lubricant and motor life. Cooling air is exhausted through a single port at the top of the cabinet. Ducting this air enables heat recovery and further reduces noise.
Air for compression enters through a separate grill on the right side of the cabinet. It is then filtered through a twostage air intake filter. This filter protects the airend and extends fluid change intervals.

This also results in much lower approach temperatures, improving moisture separation and air quality.
To increase reliability and reduce maintenance costs, the coolers are conveniently located on the outside of the unit, where dust and dirt build-up are easily seen and can be removed without dismantling the cooler. Top exhaust allows for easy heat recovery and reduces the system footprint.

rag_responses.question: Does the condensate drain on the T-model dryers waste compressed air?
rag_responses.answer: The condensate drain on the KAESER “T” model dryers does not waste compressed air. Drawing ambient air directly across the coolers and motor through separate zones eliminates preheating and results in longer lubricant life and a cooler running motor. This also results in much lower approach temperatures, improving moisture separation and air quality.

Optimized air flow design
Air is drawn into separate cooling zones for the drive motor and coolers. This "split cooling" design eliminates preheating, increasing cooling efficiency without increasing power consumption. Cooler temperatures also promote longer lubricant and motor life. Cooling air is exhausted through a single port at the top of the cabinet. Ducting this air enables heat recovery and further reduces noise.
